Article Title: HarperCollins to publish Sonia Gandhi’s controversial memoir
Article Text:
HarperCollins to publish former Congress chief Sonia Gandhi's memoir after Penguin backs out

NEW DELHI: So, who does Sonia Gandhi’s controversial memoir ‘Belonging’ belong to? HarperCollins India has stepped in to publish the Congress leader’s memoir, ending weeks of uncertainty over who would carry the domestic edition after Penguin Random House India (PRHI) exited the deal over some changes to the text. The book will hit Indian shelves on November 10, 2026 — the same day as its international release.Billed as one of the most anticipated political memoirs in recent years, Belonging is described as a personal account of love, identity, duty and belonging, offering an insider's perspective on India's political journey through Gandhi's own eyes.The HarperCollins announcement comes on the heels of a public controversy over PRHI's departure from the project, which Congress leaders have framed as an act of political censorship. Party leader Ashok Gehlot alleged that pressure had been exerted on Penguin to edit out sections dealing with Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the RSS, and China's occupation of Indian territory during Modi's tenure, calling the episode a "murder of democracy.Penguin pushed back on that framing, maintaining that it retained the right to fact-check manuscripts and suggest edits to authors, and said it remained open to publishing the book.The company had earlier this year also halted distribution of cartoonist Joe Sacco's The Once and Future Riot, about the Muzaffarnagar riots — a decision critics have pointed to as part of a pattern.Adding a layer of intrigue to the row was the fact that Alfred A. Knopf, the memoir's American publisher, is itself a Penguin Random House imprint — raising the question, as Gehlot put it, of why a version cleared for global release would need alteration for Indian readers. "What is the reason, or what pressure is there that what is being published across the world cannot be published in India?" he asked.
Article Summary: HarperCollins India has stepped in to publish the Congress leader’s memoir. The book will hit Indian shelves on November 10, 2026 — the same day as its international release. The HarperCollins announcement comes on the heels of a public controversy over Penguin Random House India's departure from the project.

Article Title: Use of drugs serious concern, act on it quickly, AAIB to DGCA on AI Phuket-Delhi flight interim report
Article Text:
The final report will tell what caused the extremely rare instance of all three hydraulic systems on an A320 failing one after the other in a matter of seconds — whether it happened due to something going wrong with the hardware or software or due to some manual intervention.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) has made an “interim safety recommendation” the Directorate General of Civil Aviation urgently “take appropriate actions as deemed fit to prevent abuse of psychoactive substance” in its preliminary report into the probe of the severe turbulence on Air India’s Phuket-Delhi flight AI 2379 on Aug 4, 2026. While the probe is still on, the prelim report officially confirms that the “confirmatory (dope) test report of the pilot-in-command (PIC) was found non-negative” and that the Airbus A320 had suffered an extremely rare multiple hydraulic failure.When the “event” occurred, “initially, (the aircraft) gained 372 feet and fell by 292 feet from its assigned flight level of 36,000 feet…. seat belt signs were off. Consequently, some passengers and cabin crew suffered injuries,” the report says. The “event’s” impact on the aircraft cabin damage was such that a “lavatory commode was uprooted from its original location.”The report says in its conclusion: “Detailed investigation regarding technical and other aspects are underway. In this case, it has been observed that the PIC was found non-negative for psycho-active substance in the confirmatory test. The confirmation of use of psycho-active substances is a serious concern, and AAIB recommends appropriate actions by DGCA on priority.The preliminary report is published as per ICAO guidelines. The investigation is in progress. The final report will be published in due course.”The final report will tell what caused the extremely rare instance of all three hydraulic systems on an A320 failing one after the other in a matter of seconds — whether it happened due to something going wrong with the hardware or software or due to some manual intervention.“At 04:02:43 UTC, while cruising at flight level 36,000 feet, the aircraft’s flight control (F/CTL) system detected loss of green hydraulic system. Further, at 04:02:47 UTC, the flight control system detected loss of blue and yellow hydraulic systems. At 04:02:48 UTC, the autopilot got disengaged and a continuous repetitive chime (CRC) came. At 04:02:51 UTC, the Stall warning triggered for 2 seconds.”“The co-pilot, who was the pilot flying (PF), responded and tried to control the prevailing situation. Subsequently, PIC took over the controls. Meanwhile, the aircraft encountered an altitude upset. Initially, it gained 372 feet and fell by 292 feet from its assigned flight level of 36,000 feet during the event. At around 04:02:52 UTC, the blue hydraulic system was recovered, and few seconds later, the yellow hydraulic and the green hydraulic systems were also recovered. Consequently, this led to the recovery of the flight control surfaces. Subsequently, the aircraft operation returned to its normal operating condition,” says the report.The hydraulics on an Airbus A320 use pressurised liquid to act as the "muscles" that move heavy flight controls, lower the landing gear, and stop the wheels. The hydraulics on an Airbus A320 use pressurised liquid to act as the “muscles” that move heavy flight controls, lower the landing gear, and stop the wheelsThe cabin supervisor (head cabin crew) apprised the cockpit about the injuries suffered by the passengers and cabin crew. The flight crew assessed the cabin situation and took the decision to continue the flight to its destination, Delhi and not divert to the nearest en route airport.The aircraft cabin suffered significant damage during the “event”. The overhead ceiling panel was found cracked or deformed at various places. Most of the passenger service unit (PSU) panels were found dislocated or bent at various places. The overhead handrail was found broken, and the sealing panel was found dislocated near the 10th row. The forward right-side emergency exit handle was found broken.In a statement, Air India said: “We acknowledge the release of the preliminary report by the Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) and continue to extend our full cooperation to the investigation, including providing access to all relevant operational, maintenance and technical records. Safety remains Air India's highest priority. Our pilots undergo rigorous training, regular proficiency checks, medical examinations and other regulatory assessments in accordance with applicable national and international requirements.Following the incident, Air India has started voluntary testing of 100% of its pilots as a further step to reinforce its safety-first approach.”“The airline maintains zero tolerance for any breach of safety, fitness or regulatory requirements and will take appropriate action wherever warranted. Air India remains committed to implementing any recommendations arising from the investigation,” AI said.
Article Summary: The Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) has made an “interim safety recommendation” the Directorate General of Civil Aviation urgently “take appropriate actions as deemed fit to prevent abuse of psychoactive substance” The preliminary report into the probe of the severe turbulence on Air India’s Phuket-Delhi flight AI 2379 on Aug 4, 2026.

Article Title: India, Belgium deepen defence, clean-energy ties; to double trade
Article Text:
India and Belgium signed deals to deepen defence and clean-energy ties and agreed to double bilateral trade

New Delhi: India and Belgium signed deals to deepen defence and clean-energy ties and agreed to double bilateral trade within five years as PM Modi held talks with Belgian counterpart Bart De Wever, the first Belgian PM to visit India in nearly two decades, reports Sachin Parashar.Following the talks, Modi pitched India's 7.8% growth in the last quarter as an opportunity for the world. In a joint statement with De Wever, Modi said global conflicts were causing major upheaval, disrupting food, fuel and supply chains, and creating uncertainty across sectors."Today, India's growth story is becoming a source of confidence and new opportunities for the world," said Modi.PM Narendra Modi announced a mechanism to fast-track investment between the two countries.Belgium accounted for $4.2bn of FDI inflows from April 2000 to Dec 2025, making it the 18th-largest source of FDI into India. De Wever’s visit resulted in 10 major outcomes — five MoUs, including two to boost indigenous defence manufacturing, co-design and co-development, and another five announcements, including appointment of a defence attache in Indian embassy in Brussels.Asked whether there was any discussion on pending extradition of fugitive Mehul Choksi, who remains in a Belgium jail, MEA secretary Sibi George said law enforcement cooperation was an “important topic of discussion and an important aspect of the relationship with Belgium”.“All issues of concern and interest are discussed at all levels of our engagement ... India remains committed to ensuring that fugitives are brought back to the country to face the law,” he added.Modi said ties with Belgium had expanded beyond traditional sectors. “Defence and security cooperation is a key pillar of our relationship. Today, we agreed to enhance military exchanges and training cooperation between the two countries,” said the PM. “The agreements between our govts and defence industries will open up opportunities for defence co-development and co-production. We will also further strengthen intelligence sharing and cooperation between our agencies to combat crime,” he added.PM said unprecedented cooperation, including the recently concluded FTA between India and EU – two of the world’s largest democratic blocs – would give a boost to global stability, development and shared prosperity.The leaders also discussed Ukraine and West Asia, underlining their support for the rule of law, dialogue and diplomacy. In a joint statement, they stressed the importance of ensuring the safety and security of maritime routes and maintaining safe and unimpeded maritime shipping.“Whether it is Ukraine or West Asia, we support all efforts aimed at an early end to conflicts and the restoration of peace,” the PM added.The leaders called for closer partnerships in semiconductor technologies to create resilient and advanced technology ecosystems in both countries, with Modi saying that Belgium’s expertise in semiconductors and India’s scale complement each other.The two leaders agreed to soon conclude a migration and mobility agreement to facilitate talent mobility.Belgium also expressed solidarity with India in the fight against terrorism. De Wever condemned the attack on civilians at Pahalgam in April 2025. “Both leaders underscored their commitment to a comprehensive/global approach to counterterrorism and affirmed that terrorism, in any form and manifestation and anywhere, could never be justified and called for its perpetrators to be held accountable in accordance with the law,” said the statement.The leaders also focused on clean energy, critical minerals and reliable supply chains. “The MoU on Renewable Energy signed today will give momentum to our sustainability cooperation. In critical minerals, we have decided to enhance ties in processing & recycling,” PM said.
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi announced a mechanism to fast-track investment between the two countries. De Wever’s visit resulted in 10 major outcomes — five MoUs, including two to boost indigenous defence manufacturing, co-design and co-development.

Article Title: PM Modi takes stock of flood situation in Varanasi as water crosses warning mark
Article Text:
The Prime Minister directed the district administration to work on a war footing to provide relief to those affected

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday spoke to Varanasi District Magistrate Satyendra Kumar and took stock of the flood situation in the city as the rising water level of the Ganga crossed the warning mark amid incessant rainfall.PM Modi, who is also the Member of Parliament from Varanasi, sought detailed information from the district magistrate about the river's water level and the arrangements being made at relief camps for people affected by the floods.The Prime Minister directed the district administration to work on a war footing to provide relief to those affected and ensure that all necessary facilities are made available immediately.He also instructed officials to make immediate arrangements wherever there is an additional requirement for relief material and expedite relief work for affected people.PM Modi further directed the administration to maintain constant vigilance over the flood situation and relief operations and ensure that immediate assistance reaches those affected.The Prime Minister's intervention came as the Ganga continued to rise in Varanasi.According to the Central Water Commission (CWC), the river's water level reached 70.54 metres at the Rajghat gauge site at 6 am on Thursday, crossing the warning level of 70.262 metres. The water level was rising at a rate of 2 cm per hour.The danger level at the site is 71.262 metres, while the highest flood level is 73.901 metres.The district administration has been closely monitoring areas affected by the rising waters of the Ganga and Varuna rivers. On Tuesday, District Magistrate Satyendra Kumar and Varanasi Police Commissioner Mohit Agrawal inspected several flood-affected areas after travelling by an NDRF boat from Namo Ghat.The officials visited Salarpur, Saraiya, Konia, Pul Kohna, Dhelvaria and Sarai Mohana to assess waterlogging and the situation of residents. They also interacted with affected people and assured them of all possible assistance.The district magistrate directed officials to remain on high alert and keep arrangements ready to shift residents to safer locations. He also ordered that boats and other resources remain available for relief and rescue operations.Relief camps at the Primary School in Salarpur and Vidya Vihar Inter College were also inspected. Officials were directed to ensure adequate food, drinking water, electricity, lighting, sanitation, healthcare and security, with special attention to children, women and elderly people.
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi spoke to Varanasi District Magistrate Satyendra Kumar. He took stock of the flood situation in the city as the rising water level of the Ganga crossed the warning mark amid incessant rainfall. The Prime Minister directed the district administration to work on a war footing to provide relief to those affected.

Article Title: To impart nationalistic learning, Bengal to have 1,000 RSS-run schools within a year: Suvendu
Article Text:
Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari set a target Thursday to establish at least 1,000 schools run by RSS

KOLKATA: Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari set a target Thursday to establish at least 1,000 schools run by RSS's education wing Vidya Bharati in every district, municipality and panchayat within a year. He also suggested a plan to merge the state's four education departments into one, specifying that there would be no separate administration for madrassa education.Adhikari, who spoke at an event to mark the 74th anniversary of Vidya Bharati at Ramakrishna Mission Institute of Culture, urged the body to shoulder the responsibility of imparting what he termed "nationalistic learning". He invited its brass to the secretariat to meet officials and take the initiative forward.Bengal has 313 such schools. Nationally, Vidya Bharati runs over 12,000 schools and 10,000 Bal Sanskar Kendras. The CM said he wanted the organisation to focus on establishing more schools in Murshidabad and South 24 Parganas, alleging that "more anti-national activities take place" in these districts. The erstwhile TMC govt, he said, polluted the education environment and institutions like Vidya Bharati would need to "help the state come out of this".He accused TMC of even twisting the Bengali syllabus to divide people. "Mother was referred to as 'amma' and not 'ma'... The syllabus was created in such a way that Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar's or Swami Vivekananda's lessons remained neglected..."Invoking Syama Prasad Mookerjee's call of "ek desh, ek bidhan, ek nishan, ek pradhan", the CM said it would apply to education, too. "We won't allow an arrangement where the higher education department will look after all universities, while another department will look after Aliah University," he said. Aliah University is currently managed by the state's minority affairs department. "I felicitated the board toppers. Later, the minority affairs department sent a separate file containing the names of 27 Muslim students. I asked why? ... I have already felicitated 20 students, and they include Muslims, Jains and Buddhists."Anand Rao, a Vidya Bharati official, told TOI its schools train students in "bharatiyatwa (Indianness)" as well as puja rituals. Some run till Class 5, others up to classes 8, 10 and 12.The website of Vidya Bharati Akhil Bhartiya Shiksha Sansthan states its vision is "to develop a system of education which would help build a younger generation committed to Hindutva and infused with patriotic fervour".
Article Summary: Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari set a target Thursday to establish at least 1,000 schools run by RSS's education wing Vidya Bharati. He also suggested a plan to merge the state's four education departments into one, specifying that there would be no separate administration for madrassa education. He urged the body to shoulder the responsibility of imparting what he termed "nationalistic learning"

NEW DELHI: Union road transport minister Nitin Gadkari Wednesday urged all state govts to allow bike taxis, saying it could give employment to eight crore people.During the launch of a pilot programme — “Suraksha” — for on-the-spot free medical diagnosis and counselling for 10 lakh drivers, construction and high-risk workers involved in building highways and mines, he also said his ministry will amend Motor Vehicles Act to introduce a negative point system for drivers for traffic violations, which will result in suspension and cancellation of driving licence.The initiative will be implemented on 150-km covering Nagpur–Kamptee areas of NH-44 and mining belt in Chandrapur in Maharashtra, with a target of 10,000 people.Speaking about the programme, Gadkari sought better medical tests and healthcare for drivers and construction workers, saying that “health of our drivers is key for road safety and there is a dire need to focus on their eyecare and other health issues they face due to the nature of their work.”On the need to allow private two-wheelers, such as scooters and motorcycles, owners to allow transporting passengers, he said this will create employment opportunities in rural areas. “We have allowed this. But some states are not allowing this. Transport is a state subject. I will urge them to do so as this will give a source of livelihood to many,” Gadkari said.Highlighting the high number of deaths and violations of traffic and transport rules by drivers, the minister said that they have finalised the proposed legislation to penalise the “habitual offenders”. He said, “There will be negative points for each violation and accumulation of a certain point will result in suspension and even cancellation of licences. We hope this will instil responsible driving behaviour,” he said.
Article Summary: Union road transport minister Nitin Gadkari Wednesday urged all state govts to allow bike taxis. He also said his ministry will introduce a negative point system for drivers for traffic violations, which will result in suspension and cancellation of driving licence.

Article Title: 'Conflict will be solved by dialogue': India as US weighs sanctions on Russian oil buyers
Article Text:
Indian Foreign Minister Subrahmanyam Jaishankar speaks during joint press conference with Ukraine's Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha in Kyiv, Ukraine.

India-Ukraine trade sees resilience despite war

External affairs minister S Jaishankar on Thursday said the Russia-Ukraine conflict cannot be resolved through measures targeting oil purchases, stressing that the war will ultimately have to be settled through dialogue, diplomacy and negotiations.Jaishankar made the remarks in Kyiv while responding to a question on whether India would consider reducing its purchases of Russian oil if the United States approves sanctions against countries buying Russian oil.“This conflict, which is today in its fifth year, will not be solved because somebody is buying or not buying oil or alumina or minerals or metals or fertiliser,” Jaishankar said.“This conflict will be solved by dialogue, diplomacy, and negotiation. That is why, it is something we would encourage,” he added.His remarks came amid discussions over possible US sanctions targeting countries that continue to purchase Russian oil. India has maintained that its energy purchases are guided by national interests and the need to ensure affordable and secure energy supplies.On India-Ukraine trade relations, Jaishankar said bilateral trade spans several sectors, including pharmaceuticals, food and agriculture, fertilisers, machinery, chemicals and consumer goods.“Understandably, in the last four years, this trade has seen some disruption due to the war situation and logistical challenges,” he said.At the same time, Jaishankar said there had been “visible resilience” in trade ties, with some new possibilities emerging.“In our talks today, we will be challenged obviously by the issues of today as well as the prospects beyond, and we will be addressing them,” he said.Jaishankar also highlighted education as a longstanding area of India-Ukraine cooperation, noting that many Indian students are currently studying in Ukraine.“I take this opportunity, through you, Minister, to thank the authorities for taking care of them,” he said.Jaishankar’s remarks came during his visit to Ukraine, where discussions included bilateral ties, trade and cooperation, alongside the ongoing Russia-Ukraine conflict.
Article Summary: India-Ukraine trade sees resilience despite war, foreign minister says. Jaishankar's remarks came during his visit to Ukraine, where discussions included bilateral ties, trade and cooperation, alongside the ongoing Russia- Ukraine conflict. His remarks came amid discussions over possible US sanctions targeting countries that continue to purchase Russian oil.

Article Title: Cruise tourism gets a boost as govt clears e-group visa
Article Text:
The nationals of all 172 countries currently eligible for e-tourist visa can avail of the dedicated e-group visit visa for cruise travel (Representative Image)

NEW DELHI: As the govt focuses on positioning India as a leading global cruise destination, the home ministry has introduced e-group visit visa (cruise) for foreign tourists arriving in India on cruise vessels which follow a fixed and predetermined itinerary.The nationals of all 172 countries currently eligible for e-tourist visa can avail of the dedicated e-group visit visa for cruise travel. The latter will authorise the foreign nationals arriving on cruise ships to enter India from any of the 38 designated e-visa enabled seaports. The e-group visit visa (cruise) will have a validity of 30 days and allow multiple entry.The cruise operator or agent of the vessel will need to submit the application for e-group visit visa for international passengers via the specified portal or mobile app, three days before berthing of the vessel at the first Indian port. No fresh application will be accepted beyond this cut-off.There is no limit on the number of tourists allowed on an e-group visit visa (cruise), home ministry sources told TOI. The details of the foreign passengers — name, nationality, passport number and issue/expiry date, etc — can be uploaded in bulk on the specified portal ( indianvisaonline.gov ) or mobile app.The e-group visit visa shall contain a QR code. Passengers may use this QR code at immigration checkpoints at the port of entry and for further travel within India, as per the fixed cruise itinerary.“Easier visa and immigration procedures will encourage international cruise companies to include Indian ports in their itineraries. This will also generate wider economic benefits for ports, hotels, restaurants, transport operators, touring businesses and local communities,” said an MHA official.The govt has, since 2024, launched two major initiatives to boost cruise tourism in India, given the great potential that the country’s 7,500-km coastline and a network of 110 navigable waterways connecting 400 rivers, presents, as per a PIB statement issued in April last year. The first initiative is Cruise Bharat Mission, launched in September 2024 with the aim of doubling the cruise traffic in India by 2029 (from 4.7 lakh in 2024 to almost 10 lakh in 2029). Also, the Maritime India Vision 2030 aims to make the country a significant player in the global cruise market, covering oceanic and coastal cruises, island and infrastructure development and river and inland cruises.
Article Summary: The nationals of all 172 countries currently eligible for e-tourist visa can avail of the dedicated e-group visit visa for cruise travel. The visa will authorise the foreign nationals arriving on cruise ships to enter India from any of the 38 designated e-visa enabled seaports. There is no limit on the number of tourists allowed on an e- group visit visa.

BETTIAH: Unidentified and unusual fish swept into the Gandak river and its floodplains by floodwaters from Nepal have prompted the Bihar govt to issue a safety advisory, asking residents of West Champaran and Gopalganj not to consume or trade in such fish until their identity and safety are confirmed.The fisheries division of the dairy, fisheries and animal resources department issued the caution on Tuesday after unusual fish were found in local water bodies and low-lying areas across the flood-hit Gandak basin.Floodwaters from Nepal have entered the Gandak system, inundating several areas of West Champaran and Gopalganj. The department said fish can be swept away from ponds, rivers and other water bodies during floods and carried over considerable distances. During this movement, they may come into contact with contaminated drains, dead animals and other pollutants, raising the risk of contamination by bacteria, viruses and fungi.“Do not consume any unidentified or unusual-looking fish. Until confirmation by the concerned department, an unfamiliar fish should not be considered fit for consumption,” the advisory said.Residents have also been asked not to buy or sell unfamiliar fish caught from floodwaters or assume an unusual-looking species is safe merely because it resembles a commonly eaten fish.Anyone developing vomiting, diarrhoea, abdominal pain, dizziness or breathing difficulty after consuming such fish has been advised to seek immediate medical attention.Wildlife Trust of India director Sameer Kumar Sinha said most fish swept into the Gandak in Bihar following the Nepal floods are believed to be ‘Bagarius bagarius’, commonly known as the goonch catfish and locally called “Gochita”.He said the large freshwater catfish is found in fast-flowing rivers of India, Nepal and parts of Southeast Asia. The carnivorous species feeds on smaller fish, crabs and other aquatic organisms and often hides among rocks in deep stretches with strong currents.Sinha said local communities consume the fish, but it spoils quickly after death and may pose health risks if eaten after deterioration. He urged people to follow the Bihar govt advisory and exercise caution. The species is listed by the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) as threatened.
Article Summary: Unidentified and unusual fish swept into the Gandak river and its floodplains by floodwaters from Nepal. Bihar govt has issued a safety advisory, asking residents of West Champaran and Gopalganj not to consume or trade in such fish until their identity and safety are confirmed.

NEW DELHI: Matching handwriting on a threat note found in the lav of a diverted Air India Express international flight with that of all 40 people on board has reportedly brought a crew member under the scanner of investigating agencies.A passenger's role is also being probed. This Monday's Dammam-Delhi flight (IX 170) was diverted to Ahmedabad after a tissue paper with the words "bomb red 430" written on it and a box, both in black ink, drawn on it was found in the lav.On landing in Ahmedabad, AI Express filed a complaint with the airport police, seeking a probe into who might have written the threat note. So apart from the normal protocol of checking passengers, aircraft and baggage, handwriting tests on all the 32 passengers, four cabin crew members and four pilots (airlines send extra crew to areas impacted by the US-Iran war to handle last-minute diversions)."The agencies had asked the airline to give the same tissue paper for getting handwriting samples. Six tissues were sought for each passenger," said sources. AI Express arranged an alternate aircraft with new set of crew members that flew all the 32 passengers to Delhi on Monday-Tuesday midnight.The crew members were asked to stay back for the probe. It is learnt that of them, seven were told Thursday they were free to leave the city."The role of a crew member is being examined apart from a passenger also being under the scanner," said sources. To be sure, no one has been conclusively found to have written the threat note and the probe is on.An Air India Express spokesperson said: "We are aware that law enforcement agencies are investigating a security-related incident involving our flight operating from Dammam to Delhi on Aug 31, pursuant to a complaint filed by us. The airline is fully cooperating with the relevant agencies in the investigation. We unequivocally condemn any conduct that compromises or has the potential to compromise the safety and security of our guests, crew and operations. Appropriate action will be taken based on the findings of the investigation."
Article Summary: Matching handwriting on threat note brought a crew member under the scanner of investigating agencies. This Monday's Dammam-Delhi flight was diverted to Ahmedabad after a tissue paper with the words "bomb red 430" written on it was found in the lav.

Article Title: Nepal minister clarifies 'compensation from world' remark after flash floods - what he said
Article Text:
Nepal foreign minister denies 'compensation' claim

'Nepal, India, and China face similar climate risks'

Nepal foreign minister Shisir Khanal on Friday clarified that his statement regarding financial compensation from countries, including India, following last week's catastrophic flash floods was from the perspective of climate change and its impact in his country."Neither I nor anyone in the Ministry of Foreign Affairs or Government of Nepal has claimed or asked for compensation from India or any other country, including China or the United States," Khanal told ANI. "Our call has been for the global community to look at this disaster from the perspective of climate change and the impact it's having in Nepal."His clarification came after Nepal launched a diplomatic push to seek compensation from "major greenhouse gas emitters." Khanal had told local media that although the Himalayan nation contributes "virtually negligible" greenhouse gas emissions, it is bearing a "disproportionate share" of the consequences of climate change."We are paying the ultimate price for a global crisis we did not create... This is not a matter of charity; it is a matter of legal and moral liability," he told Kantipur TV, excerpts of which were published by The Kathmandu Post.Meanwhile, the death toll from the Rasuwa floods had risen to 1,259 as of 7 pm Thursday, according to Nepal's National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA).Khanal further stressed that Nepal, India and China share the Himalayan ecosystem and face common climate risks, calling for greater regional preparedness and international support."I've also mentioned that all three countries — China, India, and Nepal face and share similar environmental ecosystems. We are all impacted by climate change in the Himalayas as well. Our call is for all these three countries to come together to be better prepared," he added, urging the global community to recognise the broader impact of rising temperatures and climate change on vulnerable communities.He also thanked India for its swift humanitarian assistance and underscored the need for regional cooperation.India was among the first countries to assist Nepal, sending emergency rescue equipment, modular bridge components, dewatering pumps, medical supplies and other relief materials. Its first relief aircraft arrived on August 26 with 10 tonnes of supplies, followed by 37.5 tonnes on August 27 and another 10-tonne consignment. A fifth aircraft later carried an 11-member rescue team, specialised equipment and 5.5 tonnes of essential medicines.According to Khanal, India had remained in close contact with Kathmandu and was ready to provide further assistance as needed."In this disaster context, right after the disaster, we began to receive communication from Indian officials and they have provided all kinds of support and they have said they are standing ready to provide any support that the government of Nepal needs. We've been communicating as need arises and the government of India has fully supported our initiative. So in the future also, as new requirements come up, we communicate and they stand ready to provide support," the minister said.
Article Summary: Nepal foreign minister Shisir Khanal on Friday clarified that his statement regarding financial compensation from countries, including India, was from the perspective of climate change. His clarification came after Nepal launched a diplomatic push to seek compensation from "major greenhouse gas emitters" The death toll from the Rasuwa floods had risen to 1,259 as of 7 pm Thursday, according to Nepal's National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA)

Article Title: Government to allow retrofit devices for polluting trucks & buses
Article Text:
Govt will soon allow old polluting trucks and buses to be fitted with retrofit emission-control devices

NEW DELHI: In a fresh push to curb vehicular pollution, govt will soon allow old polluting trucks and buses to be fitted with retrofit emission-control devices (RECDs) that can reduce particulate matter emissions by up to 90% and nitrogen oxide emissions by 60%. Road transport minister Nitin Gadkari announced the measure Thursday, a move that will complement govt's scrappage and replacement programme for ageing heavy vehicles.Speaking at an event organised by Society of Indian Automobile Manufacturers (Siam), Gadkari said the device, developed from an innovation at IIT-Delhi, has been successfully tested. Once retrofitted in BS-IV, BS-III and older diesel vehicles, it can bring their emissions on a par with BS-VI standards. Similar devices have already been installed in diesel generator sets to reduce pollution. Gadkari said each device is expected to cost around Rs 4,000-5,000.TOI has learnt that to enable the rollout, road transport ministry will soon notify Automotive Industry Standard 228, which will prescribe technical requirements and performance standards for these devices.Gadkari also highlighted India's acute shortage of buses, saying the country has only two buses per 1,000 people, compared with the global benchmark of eight.He stressed the need for innovative public transport solutions in Tier-II, Tier-III and smaller cities, arguing that metro rail projects are often too capital-intensive to be viable in such places.Taking a swipe at bureaucratic resistance, Gadkari referred to the proposed flash-charging articulated bus system in Nagpur and said, "IAS officers think they are the only intelligent people in the country. Politicians may know only how to win elections, but they believe only they have knowledge.They keep creating hurdles, but it is my responsibility to resolve them."Gadkari also reiterated his ministry's plan to introduce a negative points system for traffic violations to crack down on habitual offenders. The proposal, which he announced Wednesday while launching the 'Suraksha' pilot programme for on-the-spot medical diagnosis and counselling of 10 lakh drivers, construction workers and other high-risk workers involved in highway and mining projects, will assign penalty points for every traffic violation. Drivers accumulating points beyond a specified threshold could face suspension or cancellation of their driving licences, he said.
Article Summary: Road transport minister Nitin Gadkari announced the measure Thursday. He said the device, developed from an innovation at IIT-Delhi, has been successfully tested. Once retrofitted in BS-IV, BS-III and older diesel vehicles, it can bring their emissions on a par with BS-VI standards.

Article Title: Peace hinges on diplomacy, not oil trade: EAM in Ukraine
Article Text:
Jaishankar's terse reaffirmation of India's position that its energy sourcing is driven by national interests

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The Russia-Ukraine conflict will be resolved through dialogue and diplomacy and not by dwelling over who is buying oil from where, said external affairs minister S Jaishankar rejecting the Western narrative that countries buying energy from Russia are bankrolling President Vladimir Putin's war.Reiterating India's stance, the minister stressed that while the responsibility of ending the conflict rested with the parties involved, New Delhi stood ready to extend any necessary assistance to facilitate peace. Jaishankar was speaking alongside his Ukraine counterpart Andrii Sybiha in Kyiv after a meeting in which he recalled PM Narendra Modi's message to Putin last week that the endless war must now give way to end of war. The minister also called on President Volodymyr Zelensky later to discuss "approaches to end the ongoing conflict".Jaishankar's terse reaffirmation of India's position that its energy sourcing is driven by national interests and the need to ensure adequate, affordable and reliable supplies came in response to a question if India would consider cutting down purchase of Russian oil because of US sanctions."It's important that you get the challenges of providing energy for 1.4 billion people at a time when the world energy situation is very difficult.Ukraine has its perspective, which we respect. And we have ours, which I would expect others to also respect," said the minister. "This conflict, which is today in its fifth year, will not be solved because somebody is buying or not buying oil or minerals or fertilisers. This conflict will be solved by dialogue, by diplomacy, by negotiations . .. and that's why it is something we would encourage."Zelensky later said that even while Jaishankar was in Ukraine, Russia launched jet-powered Shahed drones that were developed not without Iran's help. Zelensky also thanked India for its commitment to ending "this unjust war - Russia's war against Ukraine". He added, "This certainly must not be a time of war. Peace is needed. This is India's clear position."This was Jaishankar's first visit to Ukraine since he accompanied Modi for his landmark trip to Kyiv, months after his visit to Moscow. Asked if India was looking forward to hosting Zelensky, the EAM did not confirm if he was going to extend an invitation to him.He invited Sybiha to visit India, though. Jaishankar reiterated Modi's message that each passing day of conflict only means more deaths and more destruction. "Understandably, it is for the parties involved to find a way. But, if India can be of any help in any manner, we are ready, and this was the core of my discussion so far with Sybiha," he said.Among other related issues raised were attacks on commercial shipping, with Jaishankar underlining that Indian seafarers man ships of many flags and have been among the casualties. "The impact on shipping is also significantly affecting many nations of the Global South," he said.In his remarks, Sybiha briefed Jaishankar about the "escalation from Russia and systemic Russian attacks on civilian ships, ports and infrastructure" and expressed condolences for the loss of Indian lives.
Article Summary: S Jaishankar rejects the Western narrative that countries buying energy from Russia are bankrolling President Vladimir Putin's war. He was speaking alongside his Ukraine counterpart Andrii Sybiha in Kyiv after a meeting in which he recalled PM Narendra Modi's message to Putin last week.

Article Title: Smoking raises death risk by 55% in people with diabetes, global experts call for active quit treatment
Article Text:
A meta-analysis of 48 studies involving 1.13 million people found a 55% higher risk of death, while another study of about 130,000 people with diabetes found 48% higher overall mortality and 36% higher cardiovascular mortality among smokers.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Smoking increased the risk of death from any cause by 55% among people with diabetes, according to evidence reviewed in a new international consensus that calls for smoking cessation to be treated as an essential part of type 2 diabetes care. The experts say patients who smoke should be offered medicines, intensive behavioural counselling and regular follow-up instead of being given a one-time “quit smoking” warning.The recommendations, published in Diabetes Research and Clinical Practice, are the first dedicated international consensus on smoking cessation specifically for people with type 2 diabetes. They were developed by 35 experts from 13 countries, including Indian diabetes specialist Dr Anoop Misra.The consensus recommends varenicline as the first-line medicine where available, with nicotine replacement therapy or bupropion as alternatives when varenicline is unavailable or unsuitable. Medicines should be combined with structured, intensive behavioural support and repeated contact rather than brief counselling alone.The stronger approach reflects the added risk smoking poses in diabetes. A meta-analysis of 48 studies involving 1.13 million people found a 55% higher risk of death, while another study of about 130,000 people with diabetes found 48% higher overall mortality and 36% higher cardiovascular mortality among smokers.Doctors should review patients within two weeks of quitting and again at four weeks, checking blood sugar, weight, blood pressure and medicines, as quitting can alter drug metabolism and sometimes require dose adjustments.Weight gain, a common concern, should not deter quitting. In a US cohort of 10,809 people with type 2 diabetes, median weight gain within six years of quitting was 3.2 kg. Long-term quitters had lower all-cause mortality than continuing smokers regardless of weight gain, with mortality hazard ratios of 0.69, 0.57 and 0.51 for no gain, up to 5 kg and more than 5 kg gain, respectively.Smoking is also linked to kidney damage in diabetes, with higher risks of albuminuria and diabetic nephropathy. A Japanese study of 2,490 people with type 2 diabetes found insulin resistance rose with cigarettes smoked per day and fell with time after quitting.Quitting, however, can be difficult. Some patients may not recognise the link between smoking and diabetes complications, while others fear weight gain or use cigarettes to cope with stress and anxiety. The experts recommend personalised quit strategies and relapse prevention.The consensus also highlights gaps in diabetes care, where smoking cessation often remains limited to brief advice. It calls for routine smoking assessment, active treatment, metabolic monitoring and relapse prevention as part of diabetes care.
Article Summary: Smoking increased the risk of death from any cause by 55% among people with diabetes. A new international consensus calls for smoking cessation to be treated as an essential part of type 2 diabetes care. The experts say patients who smoke should be offered medicines, intensive behavioural counselling and regular follow-up.

Article Title: SC: BCI writ runs only over lawyers, not law students
Article Text:
Supreme Court Thursday ruled that Bar Council of India has no jurisdiction to discipline or regulate law students

Only parent institution can take disciplinary action, says SC

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Thursday ruled that Bar Council of India has no jurisdiction to discipline or regulate law students and quashed its letters threatening to debar Nalsar University law graduates from registering as advocates for opposing an invitation to CJI Surya Kant as chief guest at the institute's annual convocation.Despite BCI chairperson Manan Kumar Mishra pleading for closure of the issue saying that the objectionable letters to the Hyderabad institute on Aug 13 were withdrawn within hours, a bench of CJI Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said the ambit of BCI's powers, as the statutory regulatory body for the legal profession, is required to be delineated."From an in-depth consideration of the issue, we are of the opinion that Advocates Act, 1961, whereunder BCI is statutorily created, does not confer any express or implied power on BCI or state bar councils to take any disciplinary or punitive action against law students. BCI has disciplinary jurisdiction over law graduates only after they have registered as advocates," SC said.The bench agreed with senior advocate K Parameshwar who, for former Nalsar law graduate petitioners, argued that BCI does not have jurisdiction over law students, and its Aug 13 letters amounted to making deep inroads into freedom of speech and expression of students.So far as law students are concerned, it is the parent institution or the authority prescribed under laws and bylaws governing the institution who alone have the competence to take disciplinary action, if so required, against the students,” said the bench.Parameshwar said while the letter threatened to bar the registration of the Nalsar 2026 batch of law graduates as advocates, a second letter, while withdrawing the threat, directed the university to identify the students who had given the call to oppose the invitation to CJI as chief guest at the convocation. The advocate added that both letters were without jurisdiction.On Aug 14, SC stayed the operation of both letters, terming them “absolutely uncalled for”, and shielded the students and faculty ag-ainst any action by the university pursuant to BCI’s letters.BCI chief Mishra said that both letters were withdrawn subsequently.The CJI-led bench said, “Having held so, we declare all the communications of Aug 13 or subsequent modified communications to be wi-thout any authority of law.”This indictment and clipping of wings of BCI come a day after the same bench entertained petitions alleging serious irregularities in its functioning and its composition without proper elections.On Aug 14, the bench had also said BCI had nothing to do with the students’ protest against the invitation to CJI. “The students might have written a letter to me. It is a dialogue between me and students. Who are they (BCI) to unnecessarily create an issue? This action is totally uncalled for,” CJI had said.Trashing BCI’s threat, CJI had told Parameshwar to convey to the students “to get licences to practice at the earliest and begin their careers in Supreme Court. We will empanel them and give them legal aid cases. This will be our response to all those who intend to create impediments in their professional career.”
Article Summary: BCI threatened to debar Nalsar University law graduates from registering as advocates for opposing an invitation to CJI Surya Kant as chief guest at the institute's annual convocation. Supreme Court Thursday ruled that Bar Council of India has no jurisdiction to discipline or regulate law students. Only parent institution can take disciplinary action, says SC.

Article Title: Child sex abuse material on Meta: NHRC notices to IT, I&B ministries
Article Text:
Details have also been sought regarding the regulatory status and obligations of Meta

NEW DELHI: National Human Rights Commission has issued notices to the ministries of electronics and information technology (MeitY) and information and broadcasting (I&B) as part of the ongoing scrutiny of circulation of child sexual abuse material on Instagram NHRC member Priyank Kanoongo, whose bench issued the notices on Sept 2, highlighted that the inquiry was no longer confined to who uploaded objectionable content on a platform. "It also examines the extent to which the platform's own editorial and publishing systems participate in the generation, selection, circulation, amplification or monetisation of content," he said.The bench has asked whether a digital platform's legal position can continue to be treated merely as that of a passive intermediary when its systems actively generate, modify, curate, recommend, publish, amplify or monetise content.The commission has specifically asked the I&B ministry whether Meta falls within its regulatory purview as a publisher or publisher of online curated content under IT Rules, 2021 wherever the company's systems generate, modify, curate, recommend, publish or amplify content.Meta owns Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp.Details have also been sought regarding the regulatory status and obligations of Meta and the action required to be taken by the ministry under the existing regulatory framework.The notices to the minis-tries follow ones issued to Delhi Police in July after NHRC took cognisance of allegations concerning paid ads on Instagram that facilitated access to child sexual abuse material. The commission has now sought action taken reports within two weeks from MeitY and the I&B ministry.The matter arose after media reports by BBC World Service alleged that paid advertisements using terms such as "rape video" and "child video" were being displayed on Instagram to redirect users to Telegram channels where such material was allegedly offered for sale.The bench has also sought a response from MeitY regarding compliance with the provision on mandatory reporting of offences under Pocso Act 2012 and on whether the matter was reported to the special juvenile police unit or the local police. If not, MeitY has been asked to identify the officer or authority responsible and indicate the action taken for the lapse.Material placed before NHRC includes screenshots of Meta's systems which, according to the complainant, provide suggestions relating to content ideas, audience engagement strategies and monetisation methods.
Article Summary: National Human Rights Commission has issued notices to the ministries of electronics and information technology (MeitY) and information and broadcasting (I&B) NHRC member Priyank Kanoongo, whose bench issued the notices on Sept 2, highlighted that the inquiry was no longer confined to who uploaded objectionable content.

Article Title: Poverty, inequality seed delinquency in minors: SC
Article Text:
The order stands in stark contrast to the lengthy judgement by a bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and Ujjal Bhuyan on July 21

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The full benefit of protective provisions of Juvenile Justice Act has not yet been extended to children who generally develop delinquent behaviour due to having grown up in poverty and environs marked by inequality, illiteracy and discrimination, Supreme Court has said.Exonerating a minor from the charge of attempt to erase evidence in a dowry death case, a bench of Justices Prashant Kumar Mishra and Sh-ree Chandrashekhar traced in detail the history and development of JJ Act. They said because of industrialisation and urbanisation, rural folk migrated to cities and this weakened community cohesion, resulting in families losing control over their children.Writing the judgement, Justice Chandrashekhar said Wednesday, "Poverty, inequality, illiteracy and the discriminatory environment in which a child grows trigger delinquent behaviour... The rise in the number of cases coming to this court raising the plea of juvenility for the first time indicates in ample measure that there is a huge gap in understanding of the law by stakeholders."The order stands in stark contrast to the lengthy judgement by a bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and Ujjal Bhuyan on July 21 in the case 'X vs Bihar' where they held "today's children are exposed to complex information, graphic content and adult experience that were inaccessible to the previous generation".Writing the July 21 judgement, Justice Pardiwala had analysed what propelled a person to commit a crime - "It could be enmity, it could be poverty, it could be greed, it could be perversity in mind and many others..." But the bench had not mentioned inequality, illiteracy, or a discriminatory environment as grounds for a child to turn delinquent.The bench had further said, "There is no doubt that proliferation of technology and the pervasive influence of social media has altered the cognitive and psychological development of children. In such circumstances, courts as living institutions must be responsive to this reality.""The approach of courts or the juvenile justice boards dealing with a child in conflict with the law cannot remain stagnant since the legislation came to be enacted. It must bear a balanced approach towards the evolving nature of the juvenile and legitimate demands of society," Justices Pardiwala and Bhuyan had further said.Justices Mishra and Chandrashekhar said the prosecution's eagerness to bring the culprit to court and forgetting to assess the boy's age led to overlooking of JJ Act and violation of the rights of juveniles in conflict with the law."A child should not be treated as a criminal. He is a victim of the circumstances. Sometimes he is drawn to a world of crime due to socio-economic or emotional and psychological reasons. The state owes a responsibility to reintegrate juveniles in society, rather than permanently stigmatising them," Justice Chandrashekhar said.
Article Summary: The full benefit of protective provisions of Juvenile Justice Act has not yet been extended to children who generally develop delinquent behaviour, Supreme Court has said. The order stands in stark contrast to the lengthy judgement by a bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and Ujjal Bhuyan on July 21 in the case 'X vs Bihar'

NEW DELHI: Three weeks after Lok Sabha decided to send the contentious Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill to a parliamentary committee for scrutiny, Speaker Om Birla Thursday named 31 members of the panel, with BJP MP Sanjay Jaiswal made chairperson.BJP-led NDA's 19 MPs will be in the committee, while Congress has favoured members from minority communities as their representatives.Opposition parties, including DMK, which has split from the INDIA bloc, have been critical of the bill and supported concerns of Christian bodies that the bill's provisions will adversely impact NGOs run by them, a contention rejected by govt, even though it agreed to send the draft law for wider scrutiny to the panel to evolve a consensus.With many parties taking time in nominating their choices, the committee's constitution was held up. It has 21 members from Lok Sabha and 10 from Rajya Sabha, and was asked to submit its report by the last day of the first week of Parliament's winter session. However, a committee's tenure is often extended to allow it to engage in consultation with different stakeholders.NDA's members include Bhartruhari Mahtab, Nishikant Dubey and Tejasvi Surya of BJP, Sanjay Jha of JDU, Lavu Sri Krishna of TDP and Praful Patel of NCP.Congress MPs include Anto Antony, Viriato Fernandes, Hamdullah Sayeed and Christopher Manickam. DMK's P Wilson, a lawyer and vocal critic of the bill, is also its member besides NCP-SP's Supriya Sule and TMC's Kalyan Banerjee and Menaka Guruswamy, both lawyers.Critics' main argument against the amendment bill is that it allows the executive to take control of assets of an organisation if its FCRA license is withdrawn or not renewed.
Article Summary: BJP-led NDA's 19 MPs will be in the committee, while Congress has favoured members from minority communities as their representatives. DMK, which has split from the INDIA bloc, has been critical of the bill and supported concerns of Christian bodies that the bill's provisions will adversely impact them.

Article Title: Council can seek appraisals from teachers' institues: SC
Article Text:
Supreme Court Thursday underscored the importance of the quality of teachers

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Thursday underscored the importance of the quality of teachers, who play a vital role in shaping the future of the country, and held National Council for Teacher Education (NCTE) can seek annual performance appraisal report (PAR) from teacher education institutions (TEIs).A bench of Justices P S Narasimha and Alok Aradhe said the role of NCTE in ensuring quality education for children is immense and teacher education has assumed greater importance since right to education has been recognised as a fundamental right under Right to Education Act.The bench stressed that it is necessary for the council and its bodies to ensure accountability of educational institutions. It quashed the HC order which had found fault with the council's decision to seek PAR from TEIs. "We fail to understand how a regulatory measure of a statutory body, empowered to achieve planned and coordinated development of teacher education system in the country, could be restrained from calling upon TEIs to file PAR. ...it is but natural and incidental that NCTE would require the stakeholders to provide the necessary PAR," it said.
Article Summary: Supreme Court held National Council for Teacher Education (NCTE) can seek annual performance appraisal report (PAR) from teacher education institutions. A bench of Justices P S Narasimha and Alok Aradhe said the role of NCTE in ensuring quality education for children is immense.

Article Title: CEA proposes mandatory storage for solar, wind projects
Article Text:
Govt proposes phased storage mandate for new solar, wind projects from 2027, starting at 10% capacity with two-hour duration. (AI-generated image)

NEW DELHI: New solar and wind power projects may have to install battery storage alongside generation capacity from 2027, with govt proposing a phased storage requirement as part of revised technical standards for renewable energy plants.Under the draft regulations issued by the Central Electricity Authority (CEA) on Thursday, ground-mounted solar and onshore wind projects commissioned after July 1, 2027 will have to install co-located energy storage equivalent to at least 10% of their installed capacity, with a minimum storage duration of two hours.This means a 100 MW solar plant would need at least 10 MW of storage capacity capable of storing electricity for two hours, or 20 MWh.The requirement will become more stringent for projects commissioned after July 1, 2029 and up to June 30, 2031. Such projects will have to provide storage equivalent to 10% of installed capacity but with a minimum duration of four hours. A 100 MW plant would therefore require 10 MW/40 MWh of storage.The move comes as the share of renewable energy in the power mix rises and the grid increasingly has to manage fluctuations in solar and wind generation.While there is abundant renewable generation during solar hours, it can lead to curtailment due to insufficient evacuation capacity. Storage will allow surplus electricity to be stored and used during non-solar hours.More than 8,133 gigawatt-hour (GWh) of solar energy - equivalent to 1.5 days of the entire country's total power consumption or enough to power nearly 1.4 million homes for an entire year - was curtailed during the first quarter of the ongoing financial year as the grid could not absorb excess supply during daytime. “Large-scale deployment of battery energy storage systems and grid-forming inverters are crucial for integrating renewable energy into the grid,” said a new and renewable energy ministry official.The CEA has also proposed that renewable energy plants commissioned after July 1, 2027 have at least 15% of their inverters equipped with grid-forming control. All power conversion systems of battery energy storage systems will also have to have grid-forming capability.Grid-forming technology allows power electronic equipment to help establish and maintain grid voltage and frequency, which becomes increasingly important as the share of inverter-based renewable generation rises.Stakeholders have been asked to submit suggestions on the draft Central Electricity Authority (Technical Standards for Construction of Electric Plants and Electric Lines) 2nd Amendment Regulations, 2026 by Oct 4.
Article Summary: Govt proposes phased storage mandate for new solar, wind projects from 2027, starting at 10% capacity with two-hour duration. Move comes as the share of renewable energy in the power mix rises and the grid increasingly has to manage fluctuations in solar and wind generation.

It brings together communities, Panchayats, institutions and other stakeholders on locally appropriate solutions,” said the ministry in a statement.

Article Title: Rs 5,070-crore bet: Can ‘floating solar’ power India’s next renewable leap?
Article Text:
India’s floating solar push could unlock vast water bodies while boosting clean power, storage and energy security. (File photos)

From solar experiment to energy powerhouse

India’s solar energy expansion is entering a new phase, with floating photovoltaic projects emerging as a potential answer to two of the country’s biggest renewable energy challenges: limited land availability and the need for more reliable power generation.The Union government’s approval of the Pradhan Mantri Surya Sarovar Yojana (PM-SSY) on July 31, 2026, marks a major push in that direction. According to the Press Information Bureau (PIB), the scheme will support 5,000 MW of floating solar photovoltaic capacity on reservoirs and other suitable inland water bodies, backed by energy storage systems with a minimum two-hour storage capacity.With an overall financial outlay of ₹5,070 crore, the scheme will be implemented from financial year 2026-27 to 2030-31. The government says the programme could help reduce pressure on land resources, improve grid reliability and open another avenue for India to expand its renewable energy capacity.India’s solar sector has undergone a dramatic transformation over the past decade. According to government data, installed solar capacity has risen from approximately 3 GW in 2014 to 162.15 GW as of June 30, 2026, representing more than a fiftyfold increase.The expansion has been supported by large-scale solar parks, rooftop installations, solar-powered agricultural pumps, competitive bidding and policies designed to strengthen domestic manufacturing.The government said India added 44.61 GW of solar capacity in FY 2025-26, almost twice the 23.83 GW added in the previous financial year. During the same period, total non-fossil fuel capacity reached 283.46 GW, including 274.68 GW from renewable energy sources.The latest policy push towards floating solar builds on this broader expansion, while attempting to use a resource that conventional solar projects do not require: water surfaces.The PM-SSY is designed to support 5,000 MW of Floating Solar Photovoltaic projects with co-located Energy Storage Systems, according to the PIB.The storage component will have a minimum capacity of 10,000 MWh, equivalent to two hours of storage for the planned 5,000 MW floating solar capacity. This is intended to help states manage periods of peak electricity demand and address one of the central challenges associated with solar power, its variability.Floating solar panels are mounted on buoyant structures and deployed on reservoirs, lakes, ponds and other suitable water bodies. Instead of competing with agriculture, settlements, forests or other land uses, the technology allows electricity generation from water surfaces.The government estimates that India currently has around 700 MW of floating solar capacity. The PM-SSY would therefore represent a substantial increase in the country's floating solar footprint.The scheme is based on an assessment by the National Institute of Solar Energy (NISE), which estimates that India has around 102.18 GWp of floating solar potential across reservoirs and suitable inland water bodies.The attraction of floating solar goes beyond saving land. Floating photovoltaic systems can benefit from the cooling effect of water, which can improve the operating efficiency of solar panels compared with installations exposed to higher temperatures on land. Research cited in the supplied material indicates that floating systems can generate between 0.6% and 4.4% more energy than comparable land-mounted installations, although actual performance varies according to site and technology.The panels can also shade portions of water bodies, reducing exposure to sunlight and potentially lowering evaporation. This could be particularly relevant in water-stressed regions where reservoirs are used for irrigation, drinking water or hydropower.The scale of the potential benefit depends on factors such as climate, the percentage of the water surface covered and the characteristics of individual reservoirs.Floating solar can also be paired with existing hydropower infrastructure. Solar generation can use existing transmission connections, while hydropower or pumped-storage facilities can provide a means of balancing variable solar output.This combination could become increasingly important as India adds more renewable capacity to its electricity grid.India is not starting from scratch. Some of the country's largest floating solar installations are already operating or under development. The Omkareshwar floating solar project in Madhya Pradesh, located on the Narmada River reservoir, is designed for a capacity of 600 MW and is among the country's most prominent floating solar developments.Other major installations include NTPC's 100 MW floating solar project at Ramagundam in Telangana, built on an ash pond near its thermal power station, and a 92 MW project at Kayamkulam in Kerala.These projects demonstrate how floating solar can be deployed on different types of water bodies, including reservoirs and water surfaces associated with existing industrial infrastructure.The experience is particularly relevant as the government seeks to expand floating solar beyond individual projects and create a larger national programme.Floating photovoltaics are no longer a niche technology. The first floating solar installation was developed in Japan in 2007, while larger projects began appearing during the following decade. Global installed capacity expanded rapidly, rising from around 1 GW in 2018 to 13 GW in 2022, according to figures cited in the supplied material.Asia has been at the forefront of this expansion, with China developing some of the world's largest floating solar installations.In 2022, China added a 320 MW floating photovoltaic facility in Dezhou, Shandong, developed by Huaneng Power International. Earlier large projects included installations at reservoirs and former mining sites.The technology has also expanded beyond inland water bodies. Offshore floating solar remains comparatively young, but pilot projects have been developed in marine environments, including installations in the Maldives and the North Sea.The economics of floating solar have also improved. While floating projects once carried a substantial cost premium over conventional solar, costs had moved closer to land-based systems by 2020. However, the supplied research indicates that installation costs remained around 10-25% higher in 2023, largely because of additional anchoring and mooring requirements.Land availability is becoming an increasingly important consideration as India expands renewable generation.Large solar parks require substantial tracts of land, and acquiring suitable land can involve competing demands from agriculture, settlements, conservation and other economic activities.Floating solar offers an alternative by allowing electricity generation on existing reservoirs, industrial ponds, irrigation basins and other artificial water bodies.India’s conventional solar expansion has already demonstrated the scale required to meet national targets. Large projects account for 118.79 GW of installed solar capacity, while grid-connected rooftop systems contribute another 27.88 GW, according to the government.Floating solar can add another layer to this mix without necessarily requiring comparable amounts of terrestrial land.The potential is especially significant around existing hydropower reservoirs, where solar generation can potentially share transmission infrastructure and complement hydropower generation.The PM-SSY's storage component is particularly significant because India's solar expansion is moving into a phase where generation capacity alone will not be enough.Solar power is produced primarily during daylight hours, while electricity demand can remain high after sunset. Energy storage can help shift some of that generation to periods when it is needed most.Under PM-SSY, every supported floating solar project is expected to be associated with energy storage of at least two hours. The government expects this to help states manage peak demand while improving the reliability of renewable power.The combination of floating solar, existing reservoirs and energy storage could therefore create a model that goes beyond simply adding more generation capacity.In locations with hydropower or pumped-storage infrastructure, the relationship could become even more valuable. Water reservoirs can potentially function as part of an integrated renewable energy system, allowing solar generation to be balanced through stored water or battery systems.Floating solar's environmental advantages need to be considered alongside its potential risks.Partial coverage of water surfaces can reduce evaporation and sunlight penetration, potentially helping to conserve water and limit some forms of algal growth. However, extensive shading can also alter aquatic ecosystems.The environmental impact depends heavily on the type of water body, the percentage of its surface covered, the depth and movement of the water, and the design of the floating system.Marine floating solar presents additional challenges. Anchoring, mooring and installation activity can disturb sediments and potentially affect benthic ecosystems. Large installations can also alter the amount of sunlight reaching seagrass or coral habitats.This means floating solar cannot simply be treated as a zero-impact alternative to land-based solar.For India, where reservoirs can serve multiple purposes including irrigation, drinking water, fisheries and hydropower, careful site selection and long-term ecological monitoring will be important as deployment expands.The government's floating solar push comes against the backdrop of a broader policy architecture that has driven India's solar growth.The National Solar Mission, launched in 2010, helped establish long-term targets, while the Solar Parks Scheme and Green Energy Corridor programme addressed infrastructure and transmission challenges.The Solar Parks Scheme has supported 54 parks with a combined sanctioned capacity of 39,188 MW, according to government data as of February 2026.The Green Energy Corridor, meanwhile, is intended to move renewable electricity from generation-rich regions to major demand centres. The programme had enabled evacuation of 24,567.8 MW of renewable energy through strengthened transmission networks as of February 2026.Competitive bidding has also transformed the economics of solar power. The government says solar tariffs fell from around ₹18 per unit in 2010 to ₹2.44 per unit at the Bhadla Solar Park auction in 2017.The expansion is now increasingly being supported by domestic manufacturing. Solar module manufacturing capacity grew from 2.3 GW in 2014 to around 172 GW as of March 31, 2026, according to the PIB.India's solar transition is also becoming increasingly distributed. The PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana, launched in February 2024 with an outlay of ₹75,021 crore, is aimed at expanding rooftop solar among households. More than 43 lakh households had been solarised by June 2026, according to the government.In agriculture, PM-KUSUM supports solar pumps, decentralised solar generation and feeder solarisation. Nearly 11.49 lakh off-grid solar pumps had been installed, while more than 15.89 lakh agricultural pumps were covered through feeder-level solarisation, according to government figures cited in the supplied material.Together, rooftop solar and PM-KUSUM contributed substantially to distributed solar capacity additions during FY 2025-26.Floating solar now offers another form of distributed geography, not necessarily through small installations, but by making productive use of water bodies that already exist.India's solar story has moved from building capacity to integrating that capacity into a more complex electricity system.The country's Panchamrit commitments include achieving 500 GW of non-fossil fuel capacity by 2030, alongside the longer-term goal of reaching net-zero emissions by 2070.Floating solar is unlikely to replace conventional ground-mounted or rooftop solar. Instead, its significance lies in expanding the range of locations where solar generation can be developed.The government's estimate of 102.18 GWp of floating solar potential suggests that water bodies could become an important part of that expansion. PM-SSY's 5,000 MW target is only a fraction of the assessed potential, but it could provide a large-scale test of the technology.The scheme is also expected to create 16,000-17,000 full-time equivalent jobs and support domestic manufacturing of floating structures, photovoltaic cells and modules and energy storage systems, according to the PIB.If the technology can deliver reliable generation while limiting ecological disruption and managing its higher installation costs, floating solar could become an important component of India's renewable energy mix.For a country attempting to add hundreds of gigawatts of clean capacity while balancing land, water, transmission and reliability constraints, the next solar frontier may not necessarily be another field of panels on land.It could be the reservoirs already sitting at the heart of India's power and water infrastructure.
Article Summary: Floating solar panels are mounted on buoyant structures and deployed on reservoirs, lakes, ponds and other suitable water bodies. Instead of competing with agriculture, settlements, forests or other land uses, the technology allows electricity generation from water surfaces. The government estimates that India currently has around 700 MW of floating solar capacity. The scheme will be implemented from financial year 2026-27 to 2030-31.
